label: First copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1), boosted by n/h/r/z in the sequence
explanation: Fires only at step t = L+1 (recall_idx 1): the first copy-phase step, where the input is orig(0) fed back right after <DEL> and the output is orig(1). 99.99% of activations fall here, but only about 16% of these steps are active. It never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter step, or at later copy steps. Whether it fires and how strongly looks like a graded sum over the content of the original sequence. It is stronger when n is orig(1) or orig(2) (next_out=n gives 7.7x lift, out_tok=n gives 5.7x), when h or r appear later in the sequence, and for mid-length sequences (L 5-7 hold most of the mass; L 3-4 almost never fire). Top examples look like y n n n l r h. The input token itself barely matters. No compact boolean rule separates the active 16%: the best predicate gets F1 around 0.38 with mass recall around 0.88.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 (+5.93), prev_tok=<DEL> (+5.93), orig4=h (+2.98), orig5=h (+2.92), orig3=n (+2.78), orig4=r (+2.52). Lower it: to_go=1 (-5.29), orig2=d (-4.45), in_first=1 (-3.90), L=9 (-3.77).
